mcat_description.short: Bunkhouses are portable, prefabricated steel-framed accommodation cabins designed to house multiple workers or personnel at construction sites, industrial projects, and remote worksites. They are factory-built, sold per unit or per project, and available in standard sizes (10×20 ft, 10×30 ft, 40×10 ft) with customisable room configurations and amenities.
mcat_description.long: A bunkhouse in the Indian B2B market is a prefabricated, relocatable accommodation structure built on a mild steel (MS) or galvanised iron (GI) frame with insulated sandwich panel walls (PUF, EPS, or rockwool), designed to provide sleeping quarters and basic living facilities for groups of workers or personnel. These structures are manufactured off-site in factory-controlled conditions, then transported and installed at construction sites, mining camps, infrastructure projects, airports, and industrial facilities. They are available in single-room to multi-room configurations, with optional amenities including inbuilt toilets, pantry, electrical wiring, air conditioning, and PVC vinyl flooring. The dominant construction types in India are MS portable cabins, container-type bunkhouses (converted or purpose-built), and modular multi-unit labour colonies, all designed for lift-and-shift relocation between project sites.

market_context: In the Indian B2B market, bunkhouses are prefabricated portable accommodation structures primarily used as worker housing at construction, infrastructure, and industrial project sites. The dominant commercial form is a mild steel (MS) framed cabin with insulated sandwich panels (PUF, EPS, or rockwool), available in standard sizes of 10×20 ft and 40×10 ft, with the structure designed for lift-and-shift relocation by trailer between project sites. Container-type bunkhouses — either purpose-built or converted ISO containers — form a significant sub-segment, particularly for remote or long-duration projects. Manufacturers are concentrated in Maharashtra (Thane, Navi Mumbai, Mumbai), Karnataka (Bengaluru), and Gujarat (Vadodara, Ahmedabad), with pan-India delivery. Structures are engineered as per BIS/IS codes and local municipal regulations, with ISO 9001:2015 certification common among larger manufacturers. Key buyer vocabulary includes 'portable cabin,' 'porta cabin,' 'fabricated house,' 'portable house,' and 'labour room cabin' — all used interchangeably with 'bunkhouse' in Indian trade. The ability to dismantle and redeploy structures across multiple project sites is a primary commercial differentiator in this category.
